label: Single-host public-model benchmark in the OOM-limited bench court. Qwen2.5-0.5B vs Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (BF16, 290 tensors each), SmolLM-135M as a cross-dtype secondary. The comparison is at matched exactness: every method is lossless and every restored checkpoint matched the Hugging Face LFS SHA-256. No fleet or production claim is made.

manifest.label: Qwen2.5-0.5B base vs Instruct (headline pair)
manifest.note: Both checkpoints are BF16 with identical tensor names and shapes, so the instruct checkpoint can be offered the base checkpoint's corresponding tensor as a causal parent. Sizes and SHA-256 were verified against the Hugging Face LFS pointers after download.

manifest.label: SmolLM-135M base vs Instruct (secondary, cross-dtype)
manifest.note: The operator's first-choice pair. The base repository publishes F32 weights (538,090,408 bytes) while the instruct repository publishes BF16 weights (269,060,552 bytes), despite both config.json files declaring torch_dtype bfloat16. Tensor names and shapes are identical, but the dtypes differ, so no exact weight delta is possible. This pair was ingested anyway to prove the planner refuses the causal path and still restores exact bytes; it is not the headline size comparison.

corpus.selection_note: SmolLM-135M was the first-choice pair, but its base repository publishes F32 weights while its instruct repository publishes BF16, so no exact causal delta is possible. Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct are both BF16 with identical names and shapes and are therefore the headline pair.

comparison.weftfs_data_only_note: weftfs_data_only excludes the rebuildable per-commit index segments (75549540 bytes) and commit records. It is shown for transparency but is not a complete storage method, so it is excluded from the winner selection.

weftfs_per_checkpoint.note: The marginal instruct cost is the full two-checkpoint store minus a separate base-only store built with the same harness. It therefore includes that checkpoint's own commits and index segments.

residual_risks: Single host, warm page cache after download/encode; no cache dropping is available in the court, so restore times are best-case for all methods.
ZipNN ran as a whole-file byte stream with 4 MiB streaming chunks; per-tensor or delta-aware ZipNN was not run and could change its ratio.
WeftFS per-checkpoint attribution uses a separate base-only store; index segments and commits are included in the headline store total.
